battle.name: 劉苗王起義
battle.brief: 大業十年十一月乙卯，離石胡人劉苗王在河東舉兵反隋，自稱天子、劉王，眾至數萬，同期河北、山東、江淮各處起義相應。隋將潘長文連年討伐不克，最後由虎賁郎將梁德率精騎掩襲，斬劉苗王而眾散。卡面的秦連弩靠弩機儲力、腳踏連發，隋代已退居典籍與守城器械之列。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場起義交戰的兩方，是隋朝官軍與以離石胡人首領劉苗王為首的河東起義軍。隋朝方面：全國的軍事編制仍以十二衛與各軍府為骨幹，府兵在文帝時尚能按期番上，到煬帝時因連年征高句麗、興造東都與江都的宮室、漕轉相連而崩壞，兵源改以募兵為主，郡縣的團兵、鄉兵也被推上戰線；鎮壓地方起義多由行軍總管、驍騎將軍、虎賁郎將率領臨時編成的討平軍，後方靠河東各郡的宿衛與徵發的民夫支應，糧秣沿永濟渠與汾水、黃河的水運線北運。虎賁是隋代中央的近衛精騎，領軍的虎賁郎將屬禁軍序列，出動時常是小股精騎急行，與大隊郡兵配合。起義軍方面：劉苗王是離石一帶的胡人首領，部眾數萬，成分以河東稽胡一類的邊地部族為主，也有漢人亡命與被徵兵役裹挾者；他們自稱天子、劉王，以弟劉六兒為永安王、子劉季真為太子，立了名號卻沒有九錫與百官的完整朝廷，也沒有常設的府庫與徵發制度；武裝以弓弩、槊、刀與騎射為主，缺攻城重械而善於在山地與河谷之間轉移。放在大業末年的全局看，這場叛亂是隋朝全面瓦解的一角：遼東前線吸走了最後一批精兵，河東的漕運線又因亂事而受威脅，隋廷能調動的餘力已經很薄。
countriesEn: This revolt was fought between the armies of the Sui government and the eastern Shanxi insurgents led by Liu Miaowang, a Hu chiefman of Lishi. On the Sui side the military order still rested on the twelve imperial guards and the army prefectures scattered across the empire. The fubing levies had rendered periodic service under Emperor Wen, but under Yangdi they had fallen apart through the repeated campaigns against Goguryeo, the building of the eastern capital and of the palaces at Jiangdu, and the endless hauling of grain, so that troops taken by payment replaced them as the main source of manpower while the county companies and village levies were pushed into the line as well. Punitive expeditions were normally led by a xingjun zongguan, a cavalry general or a commander of the Tiger Guards, heading a column patched together for the occasion, supported from the rear by the garrisons of the eastern Shanxi prefectures and by conscripted labour, with grain and provisions moved north by water along the Yongji Canal, the Fen River and the Yellow River. The Tiger Guards were the elite mounted guard of the Sui centre, and a huben langjiang belonged to the imperial guard hierarchy; when they were deployed it was usually a small body of picked horse moving fast, working in concert with the larger county troops. On the insurgents' side, Liu Miaowang was a Hu chiefman of the Lishi area, and his following, given as several tens of thousands, consisted mainly of the Jie Hu and other frontier tribes of the eastern Shanxi, together with Han absentees and men swept in by conscription. They proclaimed themselves Son of Heaven and King Liu, made his brother Liu Liuer Prince of Yong'an and his son Liu Jizhen crown prince, and had a name and a rank but no complete court with the nine bestowments and the full roster of officials, no permanent storehouses and no regular system of requisition. Their arms were bows, crossbows, lances, sabres and the saddlebow; they had no heavy siege engines; and they were at their best moving through hill country and river valleys. Placed in the wider picture of the last years of the Daye era, this revolt was one corner of a general Sui collapse: the Liaodong front had drawn off the last of the trained soldiers, the grain route through the eastern Shanxi was itself threatened by the rising, and the margin the court could still draw on was thin.
people: 劉苗王，本名劉龍兒，離石人，史書稱其為胡人，是隋末北方起事群雄中少數出身於邊地部族的首領。大業十年十一月乙卯，他在離石舉兵反隋，自稱天子、稱劉王，以弟劉六兒為永安王、子劉季真為太子，部眾數萬。隋廷先後以將軍潘長文率兵討伐，潘長文連年出師都不能攻下，說明官軍對這種以山寨為依托、以游擊為手段的武裝一籌莫展。最後平定這場叛亂的是虎賁郎將梁德，他率精騎出奇兵掩襲，斬劉苗王於陣中，部眾因失去首領而逐漸散去。舊唐書與新唐書都把劉苗王的事蹟記在劉武周傳中追述，並記其子劉季真、弟劉六兒的後續：劉六兒在其兄死後再度起兵，與劉武周的勢力互相策應，劉季真隨之，後為劉武周部將高滿政所殺，劉六兒最終為唐軍所平。隋朝方面的關鍵人物是煬帝楊廣與他的統帥集團：正因為大業十年第二次征高句麗的百萬大軍集結在涿郡，河東的鎮壓只能靠一支偏師與地方郡兵，劉苗王才有機會成事；也正因為劉苗王之死發生在宇文化及弒逆之前，隋廷才有餘裕收拾河東的亂局，而代隋的唐室也正是靠收拾這批北方亂源站穩腳跟。
peopleEn: Liu Miaowang, whose personal name was Liu Long'er, was a man of Lishi whom the histories call a Hu, one of the few rebel leaders of the late Sui who came out of a frontier tribe. On the yimao day of the eleventh month of the tenth year of Daye he raised troops at Lishi against the Sui, proclaimed himself Son of Heaven and King Liu, made his brother Liu Liuer Prince of Yong'an and his son Liu Jizhen crown prince, and gathered a following of several tens of thousands. The court first sent the general Pan Changwen against him, and Pan campaigned year after year without ever taking him; that failure shows how little the government army knew how to deal with a force that based itself in mountain strongholds and fought as a raiding body. The rising was finally ended by Liang De, a commander of the Tiger Guards, who led picked horse in a surprise attack, cut Liu Miaowang down in the fighting, and the following fell apart for want of a head. Both the Old Book of Tang and the New Book of Tang carry the story of Liu Miaowang as a retrospective notice in the biography of Liu Wuzhou, and record the later fates of Liu Jizhen and Liu Liuer: after his elder brother's death Liu Liuer rose again and coordinated with the rising power of Liu Wuzhou, Liu Jizhen followed him and was later killed by Gao Manzheng, one of Liu Wuzhou's commanders, and Liu Liuer himself was finally put down by Tang forces. The key figures on the Sui side were Yangdi and his command group. Because the hundred thousand men of the second Goguryeo campaign had gathered at Zhuojun in the tenth year of Daye, the suppression in the eastern Shanxi had to be carried out by a detachment and by county troops alone, and that was the opening Liu Miaowang needed; and because Liu Miaowang died before the mutiny of Yuwen Huaji, the court still had the margin to settle the disorder in the eastern Shanxi, and the Tang house that replaced the Sui stabilised itself precisely by cleaning up these northern sources of disorder.
kits: 卡面上這件秦連弩，與劉苗王起義本身並無直接關係，必須把它的來歷講清楚：連弩是弩機儲力、腳踏擊發的重型弩具，以槓桿與滑輪把拉弦的力量存進機括，擊發時再一腳踏下，連續送出多矢，較單兵上弦的普通弩機省力得多，也能在城頭或陣中維持較高的射速。相傳其制在戰國末年已見於中國，三國時諸葛亮在漢中加以損益，諸葛亮集有「亮性長於巧思，損益連弩，木牛流馬，皆出其意」之語，後世因此稱為諸葛弩；曹魏馬鈞曾依傅子所載試圖仿製而未成，說明當時連弩的機械設計仍被視為難事。到隋代，連弩早已不是軍隊的制式裝備，它更多存在於諸葛亮的兵書記載、武庫的傳聞與方技之家的演示之中；隋書的兵志仍逐一列出十字弩、符至弩等常備弩式，經籍志也仍著錄諸葛亮的兵書，可見當時的弩兵靠的是成熟的常規弩機，而不是這件古器。隋軍在河東作戰真正會帶上的是角弓與桑弓、步弩與蹶張弩、大量箭矢，護具用兜鍪、札甲、兩當鎧與明光甲，近戰靠長槊、環首刀與陌刀，騎兵有馬鎧與鐙，攻城備雲梯、撞車與飛樓，糧秣靠永濟渠、汾水與黃河的水運。起義軍這邊的裝備明顯簡陋：胡人部眾本來就長於騎射，弓弩與獵具就地可得，甲兵稀少，槊刀靠自備與繳獲，攻城器械基本沒有，跨河靠秋冬季節的淺水與小船。
kitsEn: The Qin repeating crossbow on the card has no direct connection to Liu Miaowang's rising, and its history has to be set out clearly. The repeating crossbow is a heavy crossbow whose mechanism stores the pull of the string and releases it by foot: levers and pulleys take the strain of drawing the bow into the mechanism, and the bolt is then sent by a stamp of the foot, so that several arrows can be loosed in succession. It saves the strength a soldier would otherwise spend in stringing a common crossbow, and it keeps up a higher rate of fire on a wall or in the line. Its design is said to have existed in China by the end of the Warring States; Zhuge Liang worked on it at Hanzhong in the Three Kingdoms period, and the Zhuge Liang collection contains the words 'Liang excelled in ingenious craft, and the improved repeating crossbow, the wooden ox and the flowing horse all came from his own mind', which is why the weapon is later called the Zhuge crossbow. Cao Wei's Ma Jun once attempted a copy on the strength of the Fuzi without bringing it off, which shows how hard the mechanism was then reckoned to be. By the Sui the repeating crossbow was long out of the regular establishment; it survived in the writings of Zhuge Liang, in the lore of the armoury and in the demonstrations of specialists in mechanical arts. The military treatise of the Book of Sui still lists the ordinary service crossbows one by one, with the cross-shaped crossbow and the crossbow that carries its bolt across the groove among them, and the bibliography of the Book of Sui still records Zhuge Liang's military writings, so it is clear that the crossbowmen of the time relied on mature standard mechanisms and not on this ancient machine. What the Sui army actually took into the eastern Shanxi was the horn and mulberry bow, the foot crossbow and the crushing crossbow, and a great weight of arrows; the body armour was the helmet, the lamellar and sleeveless harness and the bright plate of the Ming Guang; close fighting was done with the long lance, the ring-pommel sabre and the miodao; the horse had its own barding and stirrups; the siege train carried scaling ladders, battering rams and observation towers; and grain moved by water along the Yongji Canal, the Fen River and the Yellow River. The equipment of the insurgents was plainly poorer. The Hu people were horsemen and archers by inheritance, so bows, crossbows and hunting gear were to hand; armour was scarce; lances and sabres were personal or taken from defeated men; there were no siege engines at all; and the river was crossed by small boats and by fords in the shallows of the autumn and winter.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術是一套典型的邊地部族式的山地游擊。劉苗王據離石、石樓一帶黃河東岸的峽谷與村堡，寨柵依山脊與河曲修築，進退依附地形，堡寨之間以山谷小道相連，兵眾多不聚於一城，而是分屯於數十處山寨，隋軍即使攻破一堡，也不能斷其根本。作戰上他們避免與官軍主力正面會戰，只在官軍糧道、驛驛與郡兵駐防的空隙出手，襲擊之後即散回山中，倚仗胡人騎射的長處在丘陵與河灘之間迅速轉移，遇到隋軍大隊則退避，利用隋軍糧秣難以接濟、往返消耗的弱點把討平軍拖入消耗戰。隋軍這邊則完全相反：潘長文連年討伐而不能下，正是因為郡兵與募兵既無山地作戰的訓練，又難以在河東的山區維持糧道，兵一到就往往找不到叛軍的所在，一退又受游騎追擊。最終解決問題的是梁德率領的虎賁精騎：人數不多，卻能以晝夜兼程的急行插入山寨之間的空隙，直取首領所在，斬首而後部眾失去統屬，遂各散歸山澤。攻守之間最見效的一件兵器，是被守方倚牆而用的弩機：卡面上的秦連弩正是這一類守城器械的祖型，設於城頭與寨牆之上的弩，射程與射速都壓得住逼近的攻者。
tacticsEn: The insurgents fought in the classic manner of a frontier people in the hills. Liu Miaowang held the gorges of the east bank of the Yellow River and the country around Lishi and Shilou, where the stockades were set on ridges and bends of the river, so that movement in and out depended on the ground; the strongholds were joined by tracks through the valleys, and the troops were distributed among dozens of hill forts instead of being massed in one city, so that the Sui army could take a fort without cutting the root of the rising. In action they avoided meeting the government army in a set-piece battle and struck only at the gaps between its supply line, its post stations and the county detachments, dispersing back into the hills after each stroke, and used the riding and shooting of the Hu to shift quickly across the ridges and the shingle of the riverbank; when a formed body of Sui troops appeared they withdrew, wearing out the punitive column by forcing it to live off what it could carry and to march back and forth. The Sui army's situation was the exact reverse. The failure of Pan Changwen, who campaigned year after year without success, came from the fact that county troops and hired men had neither the training for fighting in broken country nor a way of keeping a supply line up in the hills of the eastern Shanxi; once they arrived they often could not find where the insurgents were, and when they withdrew they were chased by raiders. What settled the matter at last was the picked horse of Liang De's Tiger Guards: a small body, but able to march day and night into the gap between the strongholds and strike straight at the head of the rising, and after the beheading the followers, having no one left to obey, scattered back into the ravines and the hills. The weapon that told most decisively between attack and defence was the crossbow used by the side on the wall, and the repeating crossbow on the card is the ancestor of exactly that class of siege-side weapon: the crossbows set on ramparts and stockade walls held the assaulting party at a distance and kept up a rate of fire against it.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。這場起義的時間，《資治通鑑》卷一百八十二記在大業十年十一月乙卯，換成西曆是六一四年十二月二十七日。兵眾的規模，諸史只作「眾至數萬」的概數，《資治通鑑》《舊唐書》《新唐書》三書所載相同，沒有留下可核的實數；潘長文討伐的次數記作「連年」討之而不克，說明至少橫跨六一四至六一五兩個年度；劉苗王被梁德斬殺、眾散一事，則記於隋亡之後的追述文字之中。地理上，離石在黃河東岸、汾水下游，東距龍門渡口數十里，沿汾水南下可通絳州，順黃河而下即達龍門，正是河東防線最前出的一點；自離石至太原的道路約二三百里，糧秣全靠汾水轉運與民夫背運。隋朝的國力數字見於《隋書·食貨志》：大業中天下八百九十餘萬戶、四千六百餘萬口；《資治通鑑》記大業年間征高句麗的兵數逾百萬，永濟渠則在大業四年通至涿郡。時間跨度上，從六一四年十二月舉兵到六一八年隋亡不過三年多，而劉六兒再度起兵、劉武周攻入太原一路扯動唐室，則要到六二〇年前後才由唐軍收束。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The rising is placed by the Comprehensive Mirror, juan 182, on the yimao day of the eleventh month of the tenth year of Daye, which converts to the twenty-seventh of December 614. As for the size of the force, the histories give only the round expression 'the following numbered several tens of thousands'; the Comprehensive Mirror, the Old Book of Tang and the New Book of Tang all give it the same way, and no checkable count survives. The number of campaigns is put as 'year after year he attacked him and could not take him', which means at least that the business covered the two years 614 and 615. The killing of Liu Miaowang by Liang De and the dispersal of his men are recorded in the retrospective notices written after the fall of the Sui. In geography, Lishi lies on the east bank of the Yellow River below the Fen River, some tens of li from the Longmen ford, with the Fen leading south to Jiangzhou and the Yellow River below it running on to Longmen; it was the most advanced point of the eastern Shanxi defensive line, and the road from Lishi to Taiyuan runs some two or three hundred li, with grain and provisions carried by water on the Fen and on men's backs. The Sui's own strength is given in the treatise on food and revenue of the Book of Sui: in the Daye era there were more than 8.9 million households and some 46 million mouths in the empire; the Comprehensive Mirror records that the armies sent against Goguryeo in the Daye era numbered more than a million men, and the Yongji Canal was opened as far as Zhuojun in the fourth year of Daye. In time, from the rising of December 614 to the fall of the Sui in 618 is a little over three years, while the renewed rising of Liu Liuer and the drive of Liu Wuzhou into Taiyuan, which pulled the Tang house this way and that, were not closed until around 620 by Tang forces.
cause: 起事的原因有三層。第一層是隋廷的兵力配置：大業七年以後兩度征高句麗，第二次大軍集結於涿郡，北方精銳幾乎全部壓在前線，河東只剩下郡兵與臨時徵集的募兵，鎮壓能力降到最低。第二層是河東的漕運負擔與民生：永濟渠自大業四年開通之後，便把洛陽的糧食經沁水、汾水一路運往北方，河東沿線的民夫、牲畜與船隻年年被徵發，加上大業年間河南、河北一帶連年歉收、糧價飛漲，編戶大量流亡，郡縣的倉庫與武庫一同空虛。第三層是邊地部族與隋廷之間的舊怨：河東一帶自北魏以來即有稽胡等部族聚居，隋文帝與隋煬帝都曾大發兵員討伐他們，徵發與殺傷留下的記憶在部落之間代代相傳，隋朝對邊地的羈縻與鎮壓從未真正安撫住這批人。劉苗王出身胡人首領，熟悉部族人心，佔據黃河與汾水之間的河曲地帶，正是隋軍最難展開重兵、而胡人最利於騎射游擊的地方；他選擇的時機也恰是隋廷全部注意力壓在遼東、邊防空虛的窗口。同一時期河北的竇建德、山東的王薄、江淮的劉元進與宋子賢各處並起，說明大業十年的隋朝已無餘力同時壓住每一處的亂源。
causeEn: The outbreak had three layers of cause. The first was the distribution of the court's forces. After the seventh year of Daye came two campaigns against Goguryeo, and the second brought the great army together at Zhuojun, so that the picked soldiers of the north were almost all committed to the front and the eastern Shanxi was left with county troops and hastily enrolled paid men, the capacity for suppression falling to its lowest point. The second was the burden of transport in the eastern Shanxi and the condition of the people. Since the Yongji Canal was opened in the fourth year of Daye the grain of Luoyang had been carried north by way of the Qin and Fen rivers, and the labour, draught animals and boats of the districts along that line were levied year after year; on top of that the harvests failed for several successive years in Henan and in the north during the Daye era, the price of grain ran away upwards, and the registered households fled in great numbers, leaving the county granaries and the county armouries empty together. The third was the old grudge between the frontier tribes and the Sui court. Since the Northern Wei the Jie Hu and other peoples had settled in the eastern Shanxi, and both Emperor Wen and Yangdi had raised large bodies of men against them; the memory of the conscription and of the killing was passed on from generation to generation among the tribes, and the Sui had never truly settled those people by its system of control and pacification. Liu Miaowang, who came from a family of Hu chiefs, understood the temper of the tribes and took up a position in the bends of the Yellow River and the Fen, precisely where the Sui army found it hardest to deploy heavy troops and where the Hu were at their best on horse and bow. The moment he chose was also the window in which the court's whole attention was fixed on Liaodong and the frontier was empty. In the same years Dou Jiande in the north, Wang Bo in Shandong, and Liu Yuanjin and Song Zixian in the Jianghuai rose one after another, which shows that in the tenth year of Daye the Sui had no margin left to hold down every outbreak at once.
impact: 這場叛亂的直接效果，是隋廷在河東勉強挽住了崩壞的防線：劉苗王被斬、眾散之後，汾水與永濟渠的漕運線暫時恢復通暢，河東的郡縣重歸官府之手，隋朝得以把最後的注意力投向遼東的第三次征高句麗。這一點在當時看似保住了王朝的基業，卻正好把王朝推向了斷崖：六一五年百萬大軍再集涿郡，遠征未及而宇文化及在軍中弒逆，隋煬帝死於江都，隋朝在三年內傾覆。長遠的影響則落在河東的權力真空上。劉苗王的殘部並未真正消失，其弟劉六兒再度起兵，與劉武周的勢力互相策應，劉季真亦在其間；劉武周趁隋朝崩潰之機攻入晉陽與太原，一度威脅唐室的發祥之地，逼得唐高祖放棄關中經營而準備東遷。可以說，李世民在渭北、洛陽一線與宋金剛在河東的對峙，最早的線頭正是這場發生在離石山地的起義。兵器史的層面，劉苗王之亂也說明了一件事：像秦連弩這樣在典籍中被神化的古器，到隋代已難以回到戰場，決定勝負的仍是常備弩機、甲兵與糧道的實際供應。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the rising was that the court managed to hold the line in the eastern Shanxi as the Sui came apart. After Liu Miaowang was killed and his men scattered, the grain route along the Fen and the Yongji Canal was restored for the time, and the prefectures of the east returned to the hands of the officials, so that the Sui could turn its last attention towards the third campaign against Goguryeo in Liaodong. At the time this looked like the saving of the dynasty; in fact it drove the dynasty over the edge. In 615 the million-strong army gathered at Zhuojun again, and before the campaign was under way Yuwen Huaji murdered Yangdi in the camp, and the Sui collapsed within three years. In the longer run the effect fell on the power vacuum in the east. The followers of Liu Miaowang did not simply disappear: his brother Liu Liuer rose again and coordinated with the rising power of Liu Wuzhou, and Liu Jizhen was drawn in with him. Taking advantage of the collapse of the Sui, Liu Wuzhou drove into Jinyang and Taiyuan and for a time threatened the place where the Tang house had begun, forcing the founder of the Tang to give up his footing in Guanzhong and prepare to move east. One may say that the confrontation between Li Shimin on the north bank of the Wei and in the line of Luoyang and Song Jingang in the east of the Shanxi has its earliest thread in this rising in the hills of Lishi. At the level of the history of arms, the rising of Liu Miaowang also shows one thing: an ancient machine immortalised in the classics, such as the Qin repeating crossbow, could hardly return to the battlefield by the Sui, and what decided such a war was the actual supply of ordinary crossbow mechanisms, of armour and of the food line.
result: 劉苗王起義的結局是短促而清楚的：隋將潘長文連年討伐不克，虎賁郎將梁德以精騎掩襲，斬劉苗王於軍中，部眾失去首領後逐漸散去，這場捲入數萬人的叛亂在隋朝崩潰之前就結束了。劉苗王本人沒有建立任何政權，也沒有留下可考的結局；其弟劉六兒與子劉季真在舊唐書、新唐書的追述裏延續了這段故事：劉六兒在其兄死後再度起兵，與劉武周相應，劉季真隨之，後為劉武周部將高滿政所殺，劉六兒最終為唐軍所平。從全局看，這場戰爭的意義有兩層：對隋朝而言，它是一場被鎮壓成功的邊地叛亂，靠的是中央精銳出奇制勝，而不是地方軍的常規平叛，說明隋廷的鎮壓能力已集中於虎賁這樣的小支精騎；對唐初的河東而言，它又是隋末北方亂局的一個節點，劉武周正是在隋廷平定了劉苗王、自己卻在遼東與宮變之中耗盡最後一點元氣之後，才能放心地在河東舉事。舊、新唐書把這段記載附在劉武周傳裏，說明唐人正是把劉苗王這類北方小股勢力視為劉武周崛起的伏筆來理解的。
resultEn: The end of Liu Miaowang's rising was short and plain. The Sui general Pan Changwen had campaigned year after year without success, and then Liang De, commander of the Tiger Guards, took picked horse in a surprise attack, cut Liu Miaowang down in the fighting, and the following, its head taken off, gradually dispersed; a rising that had drawn several tens of thousands was over before the Sui itself collapsed. Liu Miaowang established no regime and left no traceable end to his own person. His brother Liu Liuer and his son Liu Jizhen carry the story on in the retrospective notices of the Old and New Books of Tang: after his brother's death Liu Liuer rose again and answered to Liu Wuzhou, Liu Jizhen followed him and was later killed by Gao Manzheng, one of Liu Wuzhou's commanders, and Liu Liuer was finally put down by Tang forces. In the wider view the war carries two meanings. For the Sui it was a frontier revolt that was suppressed successfully, and it was won by the central elite striking by surprise rather than by the ordinary work of a provincial army, which shows that the court's capacity for suppression had shrunk to small picked bodies such as the Tiger Guards. For the eastern Shanxi of the early Tang it was a node in the northern disorder of the last Sui years, and it was only because the Sui had put down Liu Miaowang while exhausting its last strength in Liaodong and in the mutiny at the camp that Liu Wuzhou could afford to raise his banner in the east without anxiety. That the Old and New Books of Tang file this notice under the biography of Liu Wuzhou shows how the Tang writers understood men such as Liu Miaowang: as the preliminaries to the rise of Liu Wuzhou.
